deep.reconstruction:
Context: Champs 2 (from 1982), contemporary with Pursuing Stacks and the start of Les Dérivateurs. The page sets up Cat with W = W_∞ (functors whose nerve is a weak homotopy equivalence). It tries to characterise W_∞-aspheric categories and W_∞-proper / W_∞-smooth functors by right lifting properties (RLP) against an explicit small set of functors between finite categories. That is, it tries to give 'fibration'-type notions in Cat a generating set, in the manner of a cofibrantly generated Quillen structure. The next page asks outright whether W_∞-fibrations and the matching cofibrations form a Quillen model structure on (Cat).

Top left. ∂ →i I: ∂ is the discrete two-object category {0,1}, I = Δ^1 is the interval, and i is the boundary inclusion, with a connectivity remark under it. The crossed-out note 'π_0(∂) ≥ 2' explains why ∂ is not 0-connected.

Top right: the proposed generating set.
(i) ∅ → e.
(ii) ∂ × S^n(N) → I × S^n(N). Here S^n(N) is a combinatorial model of the n-sphere as a finite category, presumably indexed by a subdivision level N running through a 'fundamental' (probably cofinal) part of an index set 𝒩. Subdivisions are needed so that functors out of the models represent all homotopy classes.
(iii) Left cones (resp. right cones) on the maps in (i) and (ii). For ∅ → e the left/right cone is {0} → Δ^1 (resp. {1} → Δ^1), which the page notes explicitly.

Lemma a). Suppose X → e has RLP against (i) and (ii).
- RLP against ∅ → e gives X nonempty.
- RLP against ∂ × S → I × S says any two functors S → X are joined by a natural transformation, hence are homotopic after taking nerves.
- If every homotopy class S^n → NX is represented by a functor S^n(N) → X for suitable N, then all free homotopy classes of maps from spheres are trivial.
- So X is connected and π_n(X, x) = 0 for all n and all x. Hence X is W_∞-aspheric.

Lemma b). If X → Y has RLP against the left cones (resp. right cones) on these maps, then X → Y is W_∞-proper (resp. W_∞-smooth). Lifting against cones on sphere-boundary inclusions makes the fibre-to-comma comparisons X_y → X/y (resp. y\X), and their base changes, aspheric by the argument of a).

Corollary (partly crossed out, rewritten). If X → Y has RLP against the full family, including the cones, then f is W_∞-proper with W_∞-aspheric fibres (resp. smooth). Hence f is universally aspheric, a 'trivial fibration' in Cat. The last lines (stained, partly illegible) seem to say that f is W_∞-proper/smooth relative to all W_∞ for which it has the stated lifting property, i.e. uniformity in the basic localizer.

Purpose. The aim is to find intrinsic, categorical (non-nerve) fibrations in Cat attached to the basic localizer W_∞. Proper/smooth functors are the Cat-analogue of proper/smooth base change. The next page applies this to p: Ch(C) → C × C, the category of arrows of C (morphisms as objects), which he suspects is a W_∞-fibration.
errors: Lemma a) as written needs the unstated fact that every homotopy class of maps from the n-sphere into the nerve NX is represented by a functor S^n(N) → X for some admissible N. This is true only with enough subdivision, e.g. via Thomason's Sd²/Ex² comparison. The definition of S^n(N) and of the 'fundamental part' of 𝒩 is not given on the page.

Lifting against ∂×S→I×S yields one-directional natural transformations. That suffices for homotopy, but the step from 'free homotopy classes trivial' to 'π_n trivial at every base point' is left implicit. It is correct, because X is connected and the orbit of 0 under the π_1-action is {0}.

Lemma b) is asserted without proof. The precise form of the cones is not specified: is it A^◁ → B^◁, or a pushout-product of A→B with the cone-point inclusion? Proper (resp. smooth) also needs stability under base change, which RLP gives automatically, but the asphericity of fibre-to-comma inclusions is not argued.

The neighbouring page asks whether W_∞-fibrations give a Quillen structure on Cat without mentioning Thomason (1980), who had already built such a structure. Thomason's fibrations are defined through Ex²N, not by lifting against these cone sets. Grothendieck's candidate class is different, and it is unclear (and doubtful) that it is the fibration class of a model structure with weak equivalences W_∞.

ideas.what: Characterising W_∞-aspheric (weakly contractible) small categories by RLP against ∅→e and ∂×S^n(N)→I×S^n(N), with S^n(N) combinatorial sphere models in Cat
ideas.modern_name: trivial-fibration-type lifting criterion in Cat; generating sets for Thomason-type structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thomason (1980, generating sets c·Sd²); Cisinski / Maltsiniotis for localizer-theoretic treatment
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks discusses asphericity and modelizers, but I do not recall this RLP criterion

ideas.what: W_∞-proper and W_∞-smooth functors characterised by RLP against left (resp. right) cones on sphere-boundary inclusions; the cones on ∅→e are {0}→Δ^1 resp. {1}→Δ^1
ideas.modern_name: proper/smooth functors relative to a basic localizer; analogous to left/right fibrations (RLP against outer horns, which are cones on boundaries) being smooth/proper
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Les Dérivateurs, Pursuing Stacks) for W-proper/smooth; Maltsiniotis 2005, Cisinski 2004/2006; Joyal/Lurie for left fibrations being smooth and right fibrations proper
ideas.where_published: Smooth/proper functors in Cat appear in Les Dérivateurs and in Maltsiniotis's exposition; the RLP characterisation via cones I cannot locate

ideas.what: Corollary: RLP against the full cone family gives a W_∞-proper (resp. smooth) functor with W_∞-aspheric fibres, hence universally aspheric
ideas.modern_name: proper (or smooth) + aspheric fibres implies aspheric (Quillen Theorem A/B in localizer form)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quillen (Theorem A/B, 1973); Grothendieck/Maltsiniotis/Cisinski in localizer form
ideas.where_published: Les Dérivateurs (proper/smooth base change in Cat), as far as I recall

ideas.what: Question (next page): do W_∞-fibrations so defined, with corresponding cofibrations, form a Quillen structure on Cat?
ideas.modern_name: Thomason model structure; model structures on Cat attached to basic localizers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thomason 1980; Cisinski (Astérisque 308, 2006) for model structures attached to any accessible basic localizer
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks discusses Quillen model structures on modelizers

missed.claim: Grothendieck characterises W-proper / W-smooth functors in Cat by right lifting against left (resp. right) cones on boundary×sphere inclusions, the cone on ∅→e being {0}→Δ^1 (resp. {1}→Δ^1). This is the Cat-level analogue of the later quasi-category fact that left/right fibrations (RLP against outer horns = cones on ∂Δ^n) are smooth/proper (Joyal, Lurie HTT §4.1.2). It ties Quillen's Theorem A/B-type properness and smoothness to a lifting-theoretic definition well before the ∞-categorical version.
missed.quote: b) Si X→Y a la RLP pour ces cônes [gauches] (resp. droits) sur ces morphismes précédents, alors X→Y est W∞-propre (resp. W∞-lisse)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A combinatorial lifting criterion for smooth/proper functors in Cat (or for any basic localizer) would give Thomason-style structures with intrinsically categorical fibrations. It would also give a bridge between Grothendieck's localizer theory and the left/right fibration formalism. As far as I know this exact criterion is not in Maltsiniotis's or Cisinski's accounts.

missed.claim: Candidate 'categorical' fibration class in Cat, defined by RLP against an explicit small set built from sphere models S^n(N) and their cones, proposed as the fibrations of a Quillen structure for W_∞. The question is left open in these notes.
missed.quote: Question Les W∞-fibrations, et les notions correspondantes de cofibrations, font-ils une structure de Quillen sur (Cat) ? (next page)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Whether such an intrinsically defined generating set gives a model structure on Cat (different from Thomason's Sd²-generated one), or at least a fibration category, seems unexplored. It relates to open questions on Thomason fibrations and on Thomason-type structures for strict n-categories (Ara–Maltsiniotis).

deep.surprise_reason: The notions (W-aspheric, W-proper, W-smooth, Quillen structure on Cat) are known Grothendieck themes developed by Maltsiniotis and Cisinski, and Thomason already had a model structure. The specific attempt to characterise proper/smooth functors by lifting against left/right cones on sphere inclusions is a notable unpublished detail that prefigures the left/right-fibration picture. But it is sketchy, unproved and partly illegible.

'partie [?] fondamentale [?] de 𝒩' may read 'partie cofinale de 𝒩' (a cofinal set of subdivision indices); uncertain.
The crossed-out note reads '[-π_0(∂) ≥ 2-]' (∂, not Δ), referring to the two-point discrete category.
In Lemma b), 'alors X→ [?] W∞-propre' should read 'alors X→Y est W∞-propre (resp. W∞-lisse)'.
The connectivity label under ∂→I is likely '0-connexe' or '(-1)-connexe' rather than '∞-connexe'; uncertain.
